Thanks for the clear ask. I’m attaching a compact worksheet (pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx) and a short SOW draft that shows two packaging paths we typically recommend:

1) Usage-first (pay-as-you-grow):
   - Token: storage priced per GB/mo, traces priced per sampled-trace unit (with discount tiers at 500GB, 1TB, 5TB).
   - No seat minimums; ideal for early-stage pilots and unpredictable spikes.

2) Slab / committed tiers (preferred for predictability):
   - Three slabs: Starter (250GB retention), Growth (1TB), Enterprise (5TB). Includes a fixed number of advanced dashboards and 24/7 trace ingestion SLA.
   - Bundled credits apply toward query-run and dashboard seats.

Two quick notes on credits/waiver: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to two months of Starter retention for pilots, or a 3-month retention fee waiver if you commit to a 12-month Growth slab.

Attaching trace-retention-metrics.csv and a compact month-by-month comparison (embedded in the pricing sheet but summarized below). High level:

Summary (months 1–12, based on your ramp profile):
- Pure usage: Estimated $63k total (month 12 approx $9.2k) — flexible but higher variance.
- Growth slab (1TB) + per-team dashboard seats (3 teams): Estimated $52k total with a 12-month commit + onboarding credit (equivalent to 2 months Starter).

Key tradeoffs:
- Predictability vs upside: slab reduces month-to-month variance and is easier for procurement, but you pay for unused capacity during early months.
- Seat model: selling dashboards per-team reduces friction for accounting and keeps slab footprint focused on retention.

If Skyline signs 12 months at Growth slab we can land at ~17% effective discount and include a one-time onboarding credit; to reach the 20% target we can either: extend to 24 months OR add a modest usage floor of 650GB/mo during months 7–12.
